questions.question: Which of the following statements are true? (Choose all that apply)

options.A: Checked exceptions are intended to be thrown by the JVM (and not the programmer).
options.B: Checked exceptions are required to be caught or declared.
options.C: Errors are intended to be thrown by the JVM (and not the programmer).
options.D: Errors are required to be caught or declared.
options.E: Runtime exceptions are intended to be thrown by the JVM (and not the programmer).
options.F: Runtime exceptions are required to be caught or declared.

questions.explanation: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared. Errors are generally serious JVM/system conditions and are unchecked. RuntimeException subclasses are also unchecked.

questions.question: Which are true of the following code? (Choose all that apply)

options.B: Immediately after two = null, no grasshopper objects are eligible for garbage collection.
options.C: Immediately after one = two, only one grasshopper object is eligible for garbage collection.
options.D: Immediately after two = null, only one grasshopper object is eligible for garbage collection.
options.E: Immediately after one = null, only one grasshopper object is eligible for garbage collection.

questions.explanation: After one = two, the first object has no references. After two = null, the second object is still referenced by one. After one = null, both are eligible for garbage collection.

questions.question: Which method is the conventional entry point of a Java application?
questions.explanation: A standard Java application starts through public static void main(String[] args), or an equivalent varargs form.

questions.question: Which statement about a Java source file is correct?

options.B: A public top-level class name must match the file name.
options.C: The file must always contain exactly one class.
options.D: The package declaration must appear after imports.

questions.explanation: If a top-level class is public, its name must match the source file name. A source file may contain multiple top-level classes, but only one public top-level class.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the compilation and execution flow?

options.A: javac creates machine code directly executed by the CPU.
options.C: javac compiles source into bytecode, and the JVM executes the bytecode.
options.D: The JVM compiles .java files only after the program finishes.

questions.explanation: javac compiles Java source into JVM bytecode. The JVM loads, verifies, and executes that bytecode, using interpretation and/or JIT compilation.
